title: Transactional Commit Engine & Canonical Service Delegation - Final Evidence Audit

fileStatus./src/services/commitEngine.service.ts: Newly created in Block 126; subsequently modified during type/lint refinement (previously not in repository)

realTransactionality.mechanismFound: Sequential asynchronous loop with try/catch and session state transition to FAILED
realTransactionality.finding: If entity write #1 succeeds and entity write #2 fails, write #1 remains in the database without atomic rollback or compensating deletion.

durableIdempotency.finding: Commit records and replay history are stored in-memory; they do not survive process restarts or cross-instance concurrency.

multiInstanceConcurrency.finding: Concurrency is enforced within a single Node.js memory space, but lacks Firestore runTransaction locking on the session document for distributed multi-instance execution.

preCommitVerification.finding: 10-point gate correctly validates session state, artifact contentHash, approval binding, and RBAC before attempting delegation.

canonicalServiceDelegation.finding: Engine performs pure orchestration delegating to tripService, driverTruckIntakeService, projectRosterService, and auditService.

blockers.title: Absence of Cross-Entity Atomic Transaction or Durable Compensation Mechanism
blockers.description: Writes are executed in a sequential loop. Partial failures leave orphaned production entities without atomic rollback.

blockers.title: In-Memory Commit Record & Idempotency Storage
blockers.description: Commit records are held in a local Map instance, lacking durable Firestore persistence across restarts and multi-container scaling.
